summary: Contestants use foundational desktop publishing skills to create marketing materials such as publications, logos, and graphics. All work is completed on-site using provided computers and software, and entries are uploaded electronically. The event is open to secondary and postsecondary students, but cannot be repeated or entered alongside Advanced Desktop Publishing in the same year.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes orientation
no more than ninety (90) minutes testing time
no more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
submission_requirements: All contestant-produced jobs completed on-site are uploaded electronically and are not printed at the national level
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Optional - Mac computer. Contestant must also bring software and extension cords
competencies: Apply skills in design, edit, and produce diverse business assets, including publications, logos, marketing materials, social media graphics, and website assets—for web, print, and mobile platforms

Integrate modern design principles & elements, responsive layout techniques, and foundational-level typography to create visually effective and brand-consistent publications across digital and print environments

Apply color theory, digital color management, and advanced graphic integration (vector illustrations, shapes, layered elements) to ensure visual consistency, brand alignment, and engagement across all publication formats
Design and produce multipage, multicolumn documents using master pages, styles, and templates for consistency and efficiency
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
No equipment, supplies or materials other than those specified for an event are allowed in the testing area
Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification
Contestants can use software templates, but creativity points may be reduced
At NLC, contestants will take the Desktop Publishing I (YouScience) certification with their contest. Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event
Contestants may not enter Fundamental Desktop Publishing and Advanced Desktop Publishing in the same year
This event may not be repeated
